need.statement: Adjusters re-read every first notice of loss and its attachments to decide which team handles it, and urgent water claims wait in the same queue as routine ones.
need.business_driver: Severe weather surges miss the 24-hour contact commitment in the state filing.
pain_points: Triage takes 11 minutes per claim according to the queue system
Urgent water claims wait behind routine claims during surges
Attachments arrive as phone photos, scanned forms and email threads

workflow.step: Claim arrives by portal or email

stakeholders.cares_about: Meeting the 24-hour contact commitment during surges
Policyholder data staying inside the Azure tenant
No writes to the claim record without review
Not having to double-check everything the tool says

data_sources.name: Claim records
data_sources.volume: about 900 claims per day, 6,000 in a surge
data_sources.notes: Sandbox API approved; production read access is still open.

data_sources.name: Claim attachments
data_sources.format: Phone photos, scanned PDFs, email threads
data_sources.notes: 200 de-identified claims reviewed: 38 percent of scans are low contrast.

unknowns.question: What share of claims does a human re-triage today?
unknowns.why: This is the baseline for severity agreement. Without it no accuracy claim can be compared with today's process.

unknowns.question: Will the product owner approve production read access to claim records for the pilot?
unknowns.why: The pilot cannot leave the sandbox without it.

unknowns.question: Does the state filing allow automated severity ranking if an adjuster confirms it?
unknowns.why: Answers whether the design needs legal sign-off before the pilot.
unknowns.answer: Compliance confirmed on 2026-11-02 that a human-confirmed ranking is allowed.

assumptions.statement: Severity can be judged from the claim text and attachments alone, without calling the adjuster's notes.
assumptions.if_wrong: Accuracy stays below the floor and the approach changes to rules plus manual review.

assumptions.statement: Adjusters will accept a suggested severity after reading a two-line reason.
assumptions.if_wrong: Time saved falls to near zero because adjusters re-read everything.

metrics.name: Triage minutes per claim
metrics.how_measured: Queue timestamps in the pilot group against a matched control group

metrics.name: Severity agreement with senior adjusters
metrics.how_measured: Blind review of 300 stratified claims by two senior adjusters

metrics.name: Urgent claims missed
metrics.how_measured: Weekly audit sample of claims ranked non-urgent

metrics.name: Model cost per claim
metrics.how_measured: Metered token cost divided by claims processed

value.hypothesis: If triage falls from 11 to about 4 minutes, surge backlogs clear within the 24-hour commitment without temporary staff.
value.why: Value is high because a missed filing commitment carries regulatory exposure. Likelihood is medium because low-contrast scans and adjuster trust are untested.
kill_criteria: Severity agreement on urgent claims stays below 85 percent after two prompt and retrieval iterations
Adjusters re-read full attachments on more than half of assisted claims in the pilot
Urgent claims missed rises above the 1.2 percent baseline

qualification.why: Triage is a fixed sequence: read, extract, rank and explain. Nothing needs the model to choose its own steps, so a deterministic workflow with model calls is cheaper to test and easier to audit than an agent.

rejected.why: The severity signal is in free text and photos, and the structured loss code is wrong in about a quarter of sampled claims.
No step needs dynamic planning, and open-ended tool use makes the audit trail harder to defend in a regulated process.
The add-on reviewed covers fraud scoring, not severity ranking from attachments.

requirements.statement: Suggest a severity and team for each new claim with a two-line reason citing the source text or image.
Policyholder data must not leave the customer's Azure tenant boundary except to a model deployment contractually covered for regulated data.
An adjuster confirms every severity before it is written to the claim.
Results appear within 60 seconds of claim arrival during a surge of 6,000 claims per day.
Every suggestion is logged with its inputs, model version and adjuster decision.

components.name: Evaluation harness
components.summary: Runs the 300-claim golden set on every prompt or model change.

components.name: Audit log
components.summary: Inputs, model version, output, adjuster decision and token cost.

decisions.question: Which deployment type should serve the model?
decisions.chosen: A regional deployment in the tenant's Azure geography
decisions.rationale: R2 requires processing to stay within the agreed boundary. A global deployment can process in any region.

alternatives.why_not: Inference may run in any Azure region, which fails R2.
Sends regulated data outside the tenant boundary.

evidence.claim: Global deployments can process inference in any Azure region; data zone and regional types constrain it.

decisions.consequences: Regional capacity can be scarcer than global, so quota must be confirmed before the pilot.

decisions.question: Workflow or agent for orchestration?
decisions.chosen: A durable workflow with model calls at fixed steps
decisions.rationale: The steps do not vary per claim, and a fixed sequence gives the audit trail the product owner asked for.

alternatives.why_not: Adds unbounded tool use and cost variance with no benefit for a fixed sequence.

evidence.claim: Agents are warranted for complex decisions, brittle rules or heavy unstructured data, otherwise a deterministic solution may suffice.

risks.statement: Low-contrast scans cause the reader to miss damage details, so urgent claims are ranked low.
risks.mitigation: Route low-confidence reads to full manual triage and measure the rate.

risks.statement: Adjusters distrust suggestions and re-read everything, removing the time saving.
risks.mitigation: Show the cited source inline and involve senior adjusters in the review panel design.

risks.statement: Production access to claim records is delayed beyond the pilot start.
risks.mitigation: Run the pilot on the sandbox API with replayed claims until access is approved.

tests.question: Does severity agreement on urgent claims clear the 85 percent floor on real low-contrast scans?
tests.method: Run 300 stratified de-identified claims through the reader and model; two senior adjusters score blind.
tests.pass_if: 85 percent or better on the urgent class, with no class of scan below 75 percent
tests.on_fail: Add the low-confidence manual route, re-run once, then apply the kill criteria.
tests.result: 87 percent on urgent claims; low-contrast scans 78 percent.

tests.question: Do adjusters accept a suggestion without re-reading the attachments?
tests.method: Think-aloud sessions with six adjusters on 20 claims each, timed.
tests.pass_if: Median assisted triage under 7 minutes with re-reads on fewer than half of claims
tests.on_fail: Redesign the reason panel; if a second round fails, stop.

tests.question: Can the sandbox API carry a replayed surge at 6,000 claims per day?
tests.method: Replay one surge day from sandbox data at full rate.
tests.pass_if: 95th percentile result under 60 seconds with no dropped claims
tests.on_fail: Queue with priority for urgent claims and revisit R4.
tests.result: 95th percentile 41 seconds, no drops, on the sandbox API.

tests.question: Does the panel route low-confidence reads to a person and refuse to write without confirmation?
tests.method: Scripted run of 50 claims including 12 low-contrast scans, with write attempts both confirmed and unconfirmed.
tests.pass_if: Every low-confidence read reaches manual triage and no unconfirmed write succeeds
tests.on_fail: Block the pilot until the route and the write guard hold.
tests.result: 12 of 12 low-confidence reads routed to manual triage; 0 unconfirmed writes succeeded.

demo.goal: Decide whether to fund the pilot.

beats.shows: A water claim arrives and the panel suggests urgent, citing the email text and a photo
beats.claim: Severity agreement on urgent claims was 87 percent in blind review
beats.disclosure: These claims are de-identified replays from the sandbox, not live claims.
beats.fallback: Recorded run of the same claim

beats.shows: A low-contrast scan is routed to manual triage instead of guessing
beats.claim: Low-confidence reads go to a person rather than producing a low-quality ranking
beats.disclosure: These claims are de-identified replays from the sandbox, not live claims.

beats.shows: A replayed surge day clears inside the 60-second target
beats.claim: The workflow carried a surge day at 41 seconds at the 95th percentile
beats.disclosure: This is a recording of the sandbox load test, not a production system.

beats.shows: An adjuster confirms and the severity is written back
beats.claim: Nothing is written to the claim without a person confirming it
beats.disclosure: The write-back is simulated because production access is not approved yet.

exit_criteria: Severity agreement and adjuster acceptance tests pass, or a named pivot is agreed

Urgent claims missed no worse than baseline for four weeks

phases.goal: Extend to all property triage teams and hand over.
exit_criteria: All teams live with triage time and urgent claims missed holding for one surge event
Customer team runs the evaluation harness unaided

Confirm the regional deployment boundary and review the audit log design.
